en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Ratnakaṇṭha Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Purple-Robed Subject, under Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Kapilavastu, the residence of the Śākyas, in the Nyagrodha Grove,
together with a great assembly.
At that time, the youth Rāhula was staying in another place.
During the middle of the night, he was suddenly terrified by a great and evil rākṣasa.
Thereupon, during that very night, Rāhula...
Surrounded by a multitude of youths before and behind him,
he departed from the city of Kapilavastu and proceeded to the place where the Buddha was.
Upon arrival, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet.
He then stood before the Buddha, weeping. At that time,
the World-Honored One, knowing this matter,
addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
Ānanda, you should know that I have a great illumination called the Jewel Girdle,
which possesses great merit and is able to provide protection for the youth Rāhula.
I shall now proclaim it; you should receive and uphold it.
For this great mantra, whether among the hosts of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas—
The hosts of asuras, the hosts of garuḍas,
the hosts of gandharvas, the hosts of kiṃnaras,
the hosts of piśācas, and the hosts of bhūtas.
The hosts of kumbhāṇḍas, the hosts of pūtanas,
the hosts of kaṭapūtanas, the hosts of all the lunar mansions and planets,
and the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals.
The four great yakṣa lords, the four great heavenly kings,
the hosts of all rishis free from desire who dwell on Mount Himavat,
and even all the bhūtas and rākṣasīs throughout the ten directions.
The hosts of mātṛkās such as Kaṇḍarī, Pāśānī, Kiṭikā, Karṇasuṣamā, Mahāhārī, and others;
the three mothers, the Ṛgmiṇīs, the Kṛttikās, and the great rākṣasīs.
And there is Hārī, the great rākṣasī of the east;
Yānā, the great rākṣasī of the south;
and Keśarī, the great rākṣasī of the west.
In the north is the great rākṣasī Muktācūḍā.
Each of these four great rākṣasīs is accompanied by a retinue of sixty.
If such a multitude hears the proclamation of the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle, [they shall be transformed].
In all places, he is able to provide protection for all sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle:
*Keṇi kṣara | keṇapate | gomi kṣara ||* One: *Keṇi kṣara* Two: *Keṇapate* Three: *Gomi kṣara*
2. dvayaṃ (two), 3. goma-pati (lord of cattle), 4. parika (encircling), 5. kṛṇi (making), 6. kṣarapati (lord of the flowing), 7.

Mahā-vardha-kṣaṇi-mi-ka-ri. The Buddha said, "Ānanda."
I have here proclaimed this Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle,
which possesses great merit. Should anyone uphold this mantra,
whatever they seek shall be fully accomplished.
All the hosts of Vidyādharas, the hosts of Bhūtas,
the hosts of Vetālas, the hosts of powerful devas,
and the hosts of ṛṣis endowed with supernatural powers and diligence.
It cannot create obstacles for the vidyādhara.
Ānanda, you should know that this great mantra of the precious sash has been proclaimed by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
For the benefit and peace of all sentient beings everywhere,
and even for their secret protection in all places—
Ānanda, as for those on this great earth who possess great evil, are difficult to subdue, are formidable in their majesty, and commit extremely wicked deeds.
Whether in the cardinal directions, the intermediate corners, or indeed in all places,
upon hearing this Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle, they are all greatly terrified. Furthermore,
within a radius of ten yojanas surrounding this Great Mantra, [all beings are likewise affected].
They are able to provide protection for all sentient beings,
rescuing them from difficult circumstances and sustaining them with mindful care,
so that all beings may find the cessation of calamities and abide in peace and happiness.
One shall not be struck by staffs, nor wounded by blades, nor poisoned by toxins;
all evil poisons will naturally be extinguished.
One will be kept far from evil companions and all who are malevolent.
Whatever acts of binding or confinement are performed shall be naturally liberated.
Should any human or non-human being wish to cause affliction or harm to any sentient being, [this shall likewise be nullified].
One should establish the maṇḍala according to the Dharma.
Offer various incenses and flowers to the Tathāgata.
Delimit the boundaries according to the Dharma and perform purification through bathing.
By reciting this great mantra of the precious belt,
those various evil beings will naturally be subdued and unable to cause harm;
even all suffering from illness shall be pacified and eliminated.
Furthermore, he spoke this great mantra:
*Tadyathā | nīle nīle | vimale | tamale | hūṃje hūṃje | śrī | trī | sarira*. Furthermore, Ānanda, this great mantra possesses vast merit.
When this great vidyā-mantra was being spoken,
the host of spirits who heard it were struck with terror and trembled;
the host of devas who heard it all assembled together.
If the nāga kings or the bhūta kings hear it, they will all come and assemble;
if Brahmā, Śakra, Maheśvara, Kumāra, and the other gods hear this great vidyā-mantra,
they will all come together from their various abodes to this place.
Having praised and rejoiced in the Great Mantra of the Jewel Belt,
at that time the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One..."
I shall likewise provide protection for the youth Rāhula and for all sentient beings,
performing the dharmas of guardianship to rescue them from all calamities,
sustaining and mindful of them to pacify misfortunes and bring peace and happiness.
Swords, staves, and all poisons cannot cause harm;
evil friends and fetters will naturally be cast off.
Because of these benefits, one should joyfully proclaim the Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), which says:

*Tadyathā:* (1) *avataṭe*, (2) *panate*, (3) *aninanu*, (4) *zulu zulu*, (5) *mṛdvanī*, (6) *adavanī*, (7) *samantavanī*, (8) *nirvāṇe*, (9) *nirmūne*, (10) *śānti-svastyanam*, (11) *mama sarvasattvānām ca*, (12) *loka-kuru svāhā*. At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnamekhala*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) | *Aṅguri* (2) | *Vaṅguri* (3) | *Anurī* (4) | *Nanurī* (5) | *Śikhe* (6) | *Śikhare* (7) | *Nadambhare* (8) | *Narīnarayati* (9) | *Āca āca* (10) | *Vimuca* (11) | *Śāntiṃ siddhyānāṃ kuru* (12) | *Mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca svāhā* (13). At that time, the Devaputra Yama...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle (*ratnakaṭīkā*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *raś-citi* (2) *praś-citi* (3) *rudira-kaḷani* (4) *gambhīri* (5) *nṛnari* (6) *muñjakeyūra-ji* (7) *śānti-svastya-nakrami* (8) *mama lokakuruṣva hā* (9). At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *dāni* (2) *dhanuṣi* (3) *sunaṇi sunaṇi* (4) *tini tinni* (5) *nṛme* (6) *sumi* (7) *namani* (8) *nami* (9) *tiri* (10) *mili* (11) *mamā sarvasattvanāśalokakāruṇi* (12) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ* (13) *yavase māmantakāruṇi svāhā* (14). After the Lord of Devas, Śakra, had spoken this Great Mantra, he said:
Furthermore, he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:

*Svate* (1) *Dhani* (2) *Dhanuṣi* (3) *Kandaro* (4) *Kṛti* (5) *Jvalī* (6) *Nami* (7) *Vikali* (8) *Śarī* (9) *Śaravati* (10) *Śānti-siddhy-ānaya* (11) *Mama sarva-sattva-dāntaka* (12) *Yavase-māpantu-bhavatu svāhā* (13). At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra...
He also rejoiced and proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnamekhalā*), saying:

*Svayateṃ* (1) *dāri dāri* (2) *dāraṇi dāri* (3) *ajite* (4) *phuru* (5) *muru* (6) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ* (7) *mama sarvasattvānāñ ca rakṣa kuru me* (8) *yavase māṃ pātu bhavatu svāhā* (9). At that time, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnamekhalā*), which is as follows:

*Svāhā* (1) *ānala* (2) *panala* (3) *karani* (4) *karavati* (5) *karūpi* (6) *kṛtari* (7) *kṛtakapatre* (8) *ruru-mi* (9) *cakhami* (10) *acchami* (11) *pracchaśanti-svastyayana* (12) *mama sarvasattvānāṃ rakṣa-guru* (13) *yavase-mābandha-bhavatu svāhā* (14). At that time, the Deva King Virūpākṣa...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle (*ratnamekhalā*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *mārā-mārā* (2) *jvara-jvara* (3) *ṭiri-ṭiri* (4) *kiri-kiri* (5) *sambandha-kiri* (6) *śānti-svastya-yanam* (7) *mama sarvasattvānām ca* (8) *yavase mā pānta kuru me svāhā* (9). At that time, the Moon Deity...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), saying:

*Sajye te | oṃ | vande | vimale | prabhāśāri | śataraśme | sahasraraśme | pratīśāre | khanti-siddhyāna-kuru | mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca | yavase-māṃ karmasu me svāhā.* At that time, the assembly of devas...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *kuru kuru* (2) *sulu sulu* (3) *phuru phuru* (4) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ kuru* (5) *mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca* (6) *yavāsi māmantrakaṛomi svāhā* (7). At that time, the assembly of all the lunar mansions (*nakṣatragaṇa*)...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), saying:
*Om tatre tatre tatre tatre amale amale amale amale ākarṣa-vimale śānte svastyayanaṃ kuru me mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca vyādhim apanaya kuru me svāhā.* At that time, the assembly of nāgas...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *mali* (2) *mali* (3) *acali* (4) *mathe* (5) *aśumathe* (6) *bhūke* (7) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ kuru* (8) *mamā sarvasattvānāṃ ca* (9) *yavāsi mamāṃtaṃ kuru me svāhā* (10). At that time, the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnamekhalā*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *ḍṛṭha-paṭe ḍṛṭha-paṭe* (2) *ruru-dhara ruru-dhara* (3) *śāntiṃ siddhyānāṃ kuru me* (4) *mama sarvasattvānāñ ca* (5) *yavāsi mā māṃ kuru me svāhā* (6). At that time, the hosts of *piśācas*, the hosts of *piśācīs*, and the hosts of *kumbhāṇḍas*...
Likewise, he likewise rejoiced and proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), which is as follows:
*Svāhā* (1) *taptāya* (2) *valitanaptāya* (3) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ* (4) *mamā sarvasattvānāṃ ca* (5) *yavāsi mamāṃ kuru me svāhā* (6). At that time, the hosts of *būtanā*s and *kaṭabūtanā*s...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnamekhalā*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *padme* (2) *karani* (3) *udita* (4) *cūḍāmaṇi-samīraṇi* (5) *cu cu pade* (6) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ kuru me* (7) *mama sarvasattva-śokam* (8) *yavase mamāntaṃ kuru me svāhā* (9). At that time, the assembly of mātṛ-grahas...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnamekhalā*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *Kīli* (2) *Makīli* (3) *Narī* (4) *Namari* (5) *Śāntiṃ sāstadya na karomi* (6) *Mama sarvasattvānāñ ca* (7) *yavase mā pantaṃ karomi svāhā* (8). At that time, the four great rākṣasīs from the four directions...
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭaka*), saying:

*Svāhā* (1) *āne āpe* (2) *kaje* (3) *kavaje* (4) *kukule* (5) *lipi* (6) *parihare* (7) *śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ kuru me* (8) *mama sarvasattvānāñ ca* (9) *yavase māmantraṃ kuru me svāhā* (10). At that time, there was in the assembly a great rākṣasī named Rāmiṇa.
He also joyfully proclaimed the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle (*ratnakaṭīkā*), saying:
*Svāhā* (1) *Narīṇari narīṇari* (2) *Ha ha ha ha* (3) *Hi hi hi hi* (4) *Hu hu hu hu* (5) *Śigviḥ* (6).

When the rākṣasī had spoken this great mantra, she said:

He then addressed the Buddha, saying: "The great vidyā-mantra of the precious girdle that I have here explained, along with its subsidiary vidyā-mantras, serves as a protection for all sentient beings, pacifying calamities and bringing peace and happiness."
Swords, staves, and malicious poisons cannot inflict harm upon them.
All evil associates will naturally keep their distance,
remaining at intervals of one yojana, two yojanas, and so on, up to twelve yojanas.
Whether they be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas,
asuras, garuḍas, or kiṃnaras.
Whether they be mahoragas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas,
bhūtas, pūtanas, or kaṭapūtanas.
Whether it be *sakanda*, *apasmāra*, or *vetāla*,
or a quotidian malarial fever,
or a tertian malarial fever.
Even humans, non-humans,
and others who might seek an opportunity to cause them harm shall find no such opportunity;
it is impossible for them to find an opening.
Except for the obstructions of past karma which cannot be averted,
this great vidyā-mantra can cause all sentient beings to pacify all fears in all places.
Having distanced himself from all disturbances and such matters,
at that time the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"As I have taught, regarding the Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle..."
Furthermore, regarding these great mantras and the mantra-words of the retinue of the precious girdles spoken by these rākṣasīs and others,
which possess great merit, you should receive, uphold, proclaim, and disseminate them.
Furthermore, this great vidyā-mantra can also restrain all evil winds and clouds.
One who upholds this mantra can effectively protect themselves and likewise protect others;
it can provide protection for cities, towns, villages, and indeed all places whatsoever.
Furthermore, this great mantra [is supreme] among all devas,
nāgas, ghosts, and spirits, even including śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas,
non-Buddhists, brahmans, and nirgranthas.
If there are those with malicious or poisonous minds who are unsubdued,
who cause affliction and harm, or who are inauspicious,
[this mantra] is able to subdue them all so that they no longer cause affliction or harm.
It can even suppress all great malevolent planets and lunar mansions.
Furthermore, Ānanda, this Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle is the most supreme and most excellent;
it [overcomes] all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas.
Non-Buddhist practitioners, brahmins, and Nirgranthas; as well as Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Great Heavenly Kings,
the gods of the Heaven of Mastery over Desire, the sun, moon, and stellar deities, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, humans, and non-humans.
Those dwelling on mountain peaks, those dwelling at the foot of mountains,
those dwelling in the void,
and even those dwelling in every possible place.
All the various mantra-syllables belonging to the bhūtas and others—
this [mantra] is able to sever them all, for it cannot be severed by the mantras of others.
Furthermore, Ānanda, this Great Mantra of the Jewel Girdle provides excellent protection,
excellent rescue, and excellent gathering;
it is able to bring peace, the cessation of calamities, and happiness to sentient beings.
Swords, staves, and malicious poisons cannot harm them;
all evil associates naturally keep their distance,
remaining more than one or two yojanas away.
Extending even for twelve yojanas,
moreover, Ānanda, I do not see anyone in all the worlds— including gods, humans, Māras, or Brahmās—
who can transgress this Great Mantra of the Precious Girdle.
If anyone were to transgress this, it would be impossible.
Why is that? Ānanda, you should know that all Buddhas are real, the true Dharma is real, the true Saṅgha is real, true speech is real, and all the ṛṣis are real.
Therefore, there is no one who can transgress this secret dharma-gate.
Ānanda, these five kinds of reality cannot be transgressed;
the reality of the Buddha cannot be transgressed.
The Dharma is real and cannot be transgressed;
the Saṃgha is real and cannot be transgressed;
truthful speech is real and cannot be transgressed.
The assembly of Ṛṣis is truly not to be transgressed.
Therefore, Ānanda, if there are those who receive and uphold this great vidyā-mantra of the precious sash, [they shall be protected].
One shall attain freedom from all illnesses,
liberation from all bonds,
and the pacification and eradication of all evils.
They shall attain great peace and happiness, as well as the most supreme auspiciousness.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the youth Rāhula was freed from his fear.
Ānanda and the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Sūtra on the Ratnakaṇṭha Dhāraṇī* Spoken by the Buddha.
